messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — P1: Multiple pods entering restart loop on cluster inference-prod-3. Symptom: segfaults / container restarts observed across GPU-backed nodes. 60% of replicas restarted in last 5m. Pager: jamie (oncall). Runbook: https://runbook/internal/incidents/runtime-crashloop

jamie (oncall): I'm on it — taking pager. anyone on infra? pinging sasha.

sasha (infra): Looking at node metrics now. Kernel OOPS entries on gke-infer-3b: repeated: "runtime-engine[3245]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f3c2b1a3f main+0x1c9". Attaching kern.log excerpt in-thread.

jamie (oncall): Can we reduce customer impact quickly? Carlos, any customer hits?

carlos (support): Yep — top customers Acme, BrightMap, MediServe seeing errors. About 12% 500s overall for inference routes in eu-west-1 + us-west-2. I've opened tickets and messaged account reps.

noah (runtime): I pulled a stacktrace from a crashed container. Looks like a null-deref in fused attention kernel when sequence_len > 2048 on the quantized ai-large-v2 model. Repro locally with same weights. Temporary mitigation: set env `RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNEL=1` to force fallback path.

sasha (infra): Also seeing NVML/driver messages: `E/driver: GPU 0: Xid 79` repeated which correlates with device reset. Could be driver/firmware flakiness + bad vector in kernel triggering segfault.

jamie (oncall): Proposed mitigation steps — 1) shift traffic to inference-prod-2 (regional fallback) 2) scale inference-prod-3 down to 0 replicas 3) deploy engine with fused-kernel disabled env 4) provide CPU fallback for critical customers. Agree?

elaine (platform): I can switch router weights and execute rollout. Will run the commands once you confirm.

jamie (oncall): Do it. Confirm when weight flip done.

elaine (platform): Executing now:
```
# preview then commit
./infra-router set-weight inference-prod-3=10 inference-prod-2=90 --dry-run
./infra-router set-weight inference-prod-3=10 inference-prod-2=90 --confirm
# scale down problematic cluster
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/engine --replicas=0 -l cluster=inference-prod-3
# apply env disable for hotfix image (we will restart after image deployed)
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/engine RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNEL=1 --record
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/engine
```

noah (runtime): Building a hotfix image with an extra guard at fused-kernel entrypoint. Tagging `runtime-engine:hotfix-201999` and pushing. Will update helm to use this tag.

sasha (infra): For nodes suspected of driver corruption, plan to cordon & reboot gke-infer-3b. Commands:
```
gcloud compute instances stop gke-infer-3b --zone=us-west2-b
kubectl cordon gke-infer-3b
kubectl drain gke-infer-3b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Note: draining after scaling down will reduce churn.

carlos (support): Notifying customers: Acme agreed to traffic move. BrightMap concerned, requesting SLA credit. MediServe (EU) impacted ~25% for ~12 minutes until routing change. Tickets created.

jamie (oncall): Observability update: after weight flip error-rate dropped from 12% -> 2% within 2m. Hotfix image rolled to prod-3; 6/8 pods restarted healthy, 2/8 still crashlooping on node gke-infer-3b.

noah (runtime): Those 2 crashloops correlate with GPU Xid 79 on gke-infer-3b. I think driver state is corrupted; rebooting node should clear.

sasha (infra): Rebooting gke-infer-3b now (ETA ~3m).

deploy-bot: deployment runtime-engine:hotfix-201999 rollout status: SUCCESS — rollout finished for cluster inference-prod-3 (6/8 ready reported then two pending due to node issues).

sasha (infra): Node reboot finished. Pods rescheduled, crashloops stopped. GPU Xid messages ceased. System metrics and latency back to baseline.

jamie (oncall): Quick summary for handoff: probable root cause — null-deref in fused-attention kernel path triggered by certain sequence shapes on quantized weights; issue amplified by intermittent GPU driver instability (Xid 79) causing node-specific crashloops. Actions taken: rerouted traffic to prod-2, scaled down prod-3, pushed hotfix image with fused-kernel guard + env disable, cordoned/rebooted affected node, customer notifications sent, support tickets opened. Impact: ~12% request failures at peak; critical customers notified and some requiring SLA follow-up. Next steps: runtime to bisect commit and add guarded unit tests; infra to verify driver versions and consider node replacement; support to close customer tickets with remediation notes.

jamie (oncall): Handoff to night oncall @elaine — please take 1h watch and confirm postmortem and CRs are created. Tagging for postmortem: @noah @sasha @carlos @elaine

elaine (platform): Acknowledged. I'll own the initial postmortem doc and follow up with release-blocking PRs. Links?

noah (runtime): Reproducer & traces: https://internal-artifacts/runtime/hotfix-201999/trace.txt and small repro script uploaded: https://gist.internal/repro-fuse-kernel.sh. I'll open a bisect PR.

carlos (support): Customer incident IDs: INC-5421 (Acme), INC-5422 (BrightMap), INC-5423 (MediServe). Support notes added to each.

jamie (oncall): Thanks everyone — closing pager for now. :white_check_mark: Please keep updates in this thread if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Pager closed by jamie at 2019995100.
